{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABYsmf_w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhCReyo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 21, "title": "Implement simulated WebXR bounded-floor reference spaces", "body": "## Problem

The WebXR emulator supports `viewer`, `local`, `local-floor`, and a fixed-origin `unbounded` reference space, but **`bounded-floor` remains unsupported** in Meta Quest 3 VR/MR and Generic Android Phone AR. Applications that request a room-scale boundary cannot obtain `XRBoundedReferenceSpace.boundsGeometry`; required feature requests reject and optional requests omit it.

[Issue #19](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/19) / [PR #20](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/20) explicitly deferred this because the packaged hall mesh is not an authored safe-play boundary. This Issue resolves **only bounded-floor**, without adding other WebXR modules or claiming physical guardian/room safety.

## Expected outcome

Provide a **deterministic virtual play-area polygon**, explicitly designated as the emulator's bounded-floor region, and expose it through a usable `XRBoundedReferenceSpace` on the existing immersive session profiles where the virtual floor is available.

- A request for `bounded-floor` obtains an actual `XRBoundedReferenceSpace` rather than a plain `XRReferenceSpace`.
- Its `boundsGeometry` reports an immutable/read-only ordered polygon in meters around the virtual room's floor-level origin. The polygon must represent an intentionally defined *walkable* play area, **not an arbitrary collision mesh or a promise of real-world physical safety**.
- `getOffsetReferenceSpace()` returns another `XRBoundedReferenceSpace` with the effective bounds transformed by the inverse origin offset, while pose math remains consistent with `local-floor`, `unbounded` and normal WebXR `XRFrame.getPose`/`getViewerPose`.
- Preserve correct reference-space feature negotiation and existing emulator behavior; do not require real hardware, guardian boundaries, cameras, extra extension permissions or experimental browser flags.

Use the [WebXR Device API (9 June 2026 CRD)](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/#xrboundedreferencespace-interface), specifically the [`bounded-floor` support and bounds geometry algorithms](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr/#xrboundedreferencespace-interface), as the semantic baseline. Confirm current spec status before implementation.

## Context

- Repository: `takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension`; start from `dev` and target the PR to `dev`.
- Existing source: `src/polyfill/api/geometry.ts` (`XRReferenceSpace`, origin offset), `src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts` (request/feature negotiation), `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts` (reference-space transforms and mode support), `src/devices.json`, `src/polyfill/api/environment.ts` (room triangles), `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts` (virtual floor/room), and `tests/conformance.ts` / `tests/browser-smoke.ts`.
- [Capability inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/webxr-conformance.md) notes that `bounded-floor` was deferred because the hall geometry is **not** an authored safe-play polygon. Keep the concept of the physical room mesh distinct from the emulator's configured virtual usable boundary.
- The existing floor is world Y=0 and the emulator already implements `local-floor` and `unbounded`. Prefer a small, documented polygon (for example, an intentionally chosen rectangular area entirely inside usable virtual room floor geometry), deterministic across restarts, rather than guessing safety from every mesh triangle. If the room changes, either select a meaningful matching boundary or correctly leave the feature unsupported.
- Follow the [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md) and PR template. Use English for Issue/PR bodies and review commentary.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **Author a virtual play-area boundary:** Define and document an explicit finite, non-self-intersecting, usable floor-level polygon consistent with the packaged virtual room. Confirm that its shape is valid and lies in a walkable region of the authored scene; do not equate decorative geometry or a hall's arbitrary triangles with a safety boundary. Avoid inventing actual guardian/physical-device tracking claims. A fixed polygon for the existing virtual room is sufficient; panel editing is optional.
- [ ] **Implement `XRBoundedReferenceSpace`:** Provide a public class/interface extending `XRReferenceSpace`, with a `boundsGeometry` read-only frozen array of `DOMPointReadOnly` vertices, native bounds at floor Y=0 and W=1, sensible meter coordinates and clockwise winding when viewed from above. Ensure returned points cannot be mutated by the application; implement sensible identity/lifetime semantics.
- [ ] **Implement offset semantics:** `XRBoundedReferenceSpace.getOffsetReferenceSpace(XRRigidTransform)` returns the same bounded subclass, not a plain `XRReferenceSpace`. Apply the **inverse cumulative origin offset** to the native boundary as required by the spec, including translation, yaw rotation and successive offsets, without double-transforming or changing the original boundary; verify poses and effective geometry remain in agreement.
- [ ] **Add proper feature negotiation:** Support explicit `requiredFeatures: ['bounded-floor']` and `optionalFeatures: ['bounded-floor']` only for eligible immersive profiles/modes (evaluate Quest VR, Quest MR and Android AR according to their defined floor/boundary simulation), with correct `enabledFeatures` and errors. Inline and unsupported configurations must continue to reject required or omit optional, and must not instantiate a misleading empty bounded space. Validate session ownership and ended-session behavior.
- [ ] **Preserve ordinary room movement:** The polygon communicates a simulated play area; do not silently clamp viewer poses or prevent moving outside bounds merely to make a test pass. Existing `viewer`, `local`, `local-floor`, `unbounded`, offset reference spaces, Hit Test, Plane/Mesh Detection, Anchors, controllers and DOM Overlay Preview must retain their behavior.
- [ ] **Automated API tests:** Verify native and offset bounds coordinates/winding/frozen arrays, inverse-transformed polygons, sequential offsets, independent source space, valid/invalid reference-space requests, correct `getViewerPose`/`getPose` with the bounded reference space, correct values across virtual viewer movement and profile/mode changes, and no regressions in ended-session handling.
- [ ] **Browser integration tests:** Exercise an actual unpacked MV3 extension/WebXR page in contemporary desktop Chromium, including positive Quest VR/MR and Android AR paths where supported, negative inline requests, browser startup, and a visual/demo case that renders the returned `boundsGeometry` as a floor outline. Verify that the outline corresponds to the authored virtual play region and the runtime uses the same coordinates.
- [ ] Run and record actual results of `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, `npm run test:browser`, and applicable `npm run test:wpt`/`npm run test:samples`. Separate Firefox package generation from actual Firefox runtime testing; make no physical-device/full-WebXR-conformance claims.
- [ ] Update README and `docs/webxr-conformance.md` with the feature matrix, actual virtual play-area geometry, limitations and example `requestReferenceSpace('bounded-floor')` usage. Explain clearly that boundaries are intended for developer testing only and **not real guardian/chaperone safety limits**.
- [ ] Submit the implementation PR against `dev`, following the repository PR/review guidelines and noting test results and any genuine remaining limitation. Close this Issue only once the requested bounded-floor implementation and verification are complete.

## Optional validation

- Exercise a public room-scale WebXR sample that requests `bounded-floor`, if available and reproducible.
- Add a future DevTools control for custom polygon/boundary presets; **not required** for the initial bounded-floor implementation.
- Test alternative authored room assets and concave boundaries if useful. An unchanging validated polygon for the default room is sufficient initially.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All required behavior, geometry, tests and documentation are verifiable before merge. Physical guardian/device validation and store deployment are outside scope.
